pergunta: R-F: above 30 m (ETH class), does A remain above the gap between estimators (O3) when the GEDI label is recomputed only from shots that pass the standard literature filter?
protocolo: Pre-declared design note for check R-F (not distributed).

bracos_definicao.F0: quality_flag == 1 and num_modos >= 1 + the plausibility cut of the biome
bracos_definicao.F2: F0 and degrade_flag == 0 and sensitivity >= 0.98 and beam in ['BEAM0101', 'BEAM0110', 'BEAM1000', 'BEAM1011'] and solar_elevation < 0
bracos_definicao.atl08: unchanged across the three arms (adopted criterion)

criterio.regra: supported if the three lower bounds > the O3 ceiling of the class
criterio.classe_20_30m: secondary reading against 0.500 m; floor not defined by the protocol (atinge_piso = null)

decisoes_de_implementacao: population = auditar_tabela3_dump.parquet (sha256 checked against the one recorded in auditar_rotulo_regua_v2.json); A_adotado = termo_rotulo of the dump; montar_populacao is not re-executed
plausibility limits derived once, as in the original (all approved shots of the biome), and applied equally to the three arms; Fk = F0 and the extra condition of the arm
roughness step of montar_bioma omitted: it changes neither bom nor y_novo
G1: 'no cell above 0.5 m without a recorded explanation' implemented as zero cells above 0.5 m and zero cells without an F0 shot
G3 checked to 3 decimal places (the protocol fixes 1.442 and 0.500)
bootstrap: same stream tags as auditar_rotulo_regua_v2 for A and reduction in all arms; the shift has its own tag per arm
20-30 m class: floor not defined by the protocol (atinge_piso = null); mechanical verdict against 0.500 m as a secondary reading
unit: transect only (R-F does not ask for footprint)
sensitivity > 1 not excluded (literal protocol filter); count reported
